userStories.title: Add the two fleet ask catalog keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add fleet.job.shell.escalate and fleet.budget.override with their risk, scope, default and floor rules, leaving both surfaces pending.

**Motivation** — The engine shipped for writes a principal asks for: `ApprovalGate.gate` runs a registered command at once or opens a request, and a decision is approve or reject.

**Approach** — `apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts`:
```ts
const NEW_KEY_SCOPES = {
  // ... existing ten keys unchanged ...
  'fleet.job.shell.escalate': 'project',
  'fleet.budget.override': 'any',
};
const HIGH_RISK_PREFIXES = [ /* existing */ 'fleet.job.shell.' ];
/** Keys whose decision needs the decider's input, so nobody-asked (`none`) cannot run them. */
const DECIDER_INPUT_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['fleet.budget.override']);
// buildEntry:
floor: !approvable ? 'none' : risk === 'critical' ? 'human' : DECIDER_INPUT_KEYS.has(key) ? 'self' : 'none',
```

Derived entries (US-001 AC-1, AC-2):

| Key | scope | access | risk | approvable | floor | default |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `fleet.job.shell.escalate` | project | role | high | true | none | agent |
| `fleet.budget.override` | any | role | high | true | self | agent |

Both join `PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS`: no route, tool or system writer declares them until `permissions-p3-approval-fleet`. The header comment's "plus the nine keys the design adds" becomes "plus the keys the design adds (`NEW_KEY_SCOPES`)". `catalog.spec.ts` keeps its own copies of `NEW_KEY_SCOPES` and `HIGH_RISK_PREFIXES` and its own derivation, and gains the same two keys, the prefix and the floor rule. `role-matrix.spec.ts` AC-2's column count goes from 221 to 223 and the snapshot is regenerated.

Who holds them through existing entries (the role-matrix snapshot shows it): Owner and Admin through `*`; Project Admin through `*` (both fit a PROJECT role); Developer holds `fleet.job.shell.escalate` through `fleet.job.*` but not `fleet.budget.override`. No other seeded role holds either.

**Bash asks are high risk.** By the catalog's rules `fleet.job.shell.escalate` would be medium risk (its last segment is not `delete`/`remove` and no high-risk prefix matches), so its default would be `none` and every bash ask would be allowed with nobody asked. `fleet.job.shell.` joins `HIGH_RISK_PREFIXES`, which gives the default `agent`: an agent other than the job's own, or a human, decides, as today.

**A key whose decision needs the decider's input has the floor `self`.** `fleet.budget.override` cannot run with nobody asked, because someone must choose the amount. A new `DECIDER_INPUT_KEYS` set in `catalog.ts` holds it, and `buildEntry` gives such a key the floor `self` (still `human` for a critical key). A policy can therefore never set it to `none`.

**`fleet.budget.override` is scope `any`.** A global budget policy's ask has no project; a project or repo policy's ask has one. `fleet.job.shell.escalate` is scope `project`: every job has a project.

**The floor `self` still lets an agent decide a budget ask.** A `type:AGENT` or pattern policy at `self` is satisfied by any agent holding the decide permission and the action key; that agent chooses the amount in its params. What the floor rules out is nobody deciding.

**Scope** — In: catalog derivation, mirrored catalog derivation, permission-contract expectedPending, role-matrix count and regenerated snapshot (Vitest -u from apps/api). Out: Developer's new narrowed decide seed and corresponding project decide-cell flip (US-002); resolver SYSTEM handling (US-010); opening asks (US-006); registering fleet commands or declaring new production surfaces (next feature). Switching any producer or reader to the engine, registering the two fleet commands, the adapters over `/fleet/approvals`, and dropping `FleetApproval`, `ApprovalCloser`, `ApprovalExpirySweeper` and the `fleet.approval.decide.*` keys: `permissions-p3-approval-fleet`.

**Interface** — The catalog rule declarations above are the specified interface; existing findCatalogEntry and PermissionCatalogEntry remain the consumers' interface.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.job.shell.escalate') returns an entry matching { scope: 'project', access: 'role', risk: 'high', approval: { approvable: true, floor: 'none', default: 'agent' } } using toMatchObject.

AC-2 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.budget.override') returns an entry matching { scope: 'any', access: 'role', risk: 'high', approval: { approvable: true, floor: 'self', default: 'agent' } } using toMatchObject.
AC-3 [unit, regression pin] findCatalogEntry('fleet.budget.read') still returns approval.approvable false.
AC-4 [unit, regression pin] findCatalogEntry('fleet.budget.update').approval.floor is still 'none'.
AC-5 [unit] PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS equals the set fleet.approval.decide.assistant, member.remove, fleet.job.shell.escalate, fleet.budget.override.

AC-6 [unit] The catalog spec's independent derivation returns no mismatch for any catalog key, with fleet.job.shell. in its high-risk prefixes and the self floor for fleet.budget.override in its derivation.
AC-7 [unit] Every role-matrix row has 223 cells.
AC-8 [unit] The regenerated role matrix allows Developer's fleet.job.shell.escalate cell in project p1.
AC-9 [unit] The regenerated role matrix denies Developer's fleet.budget.override cell in project p1.
AC-10 [unit] The regenerated role matrix allows Project Admin's fleet.budget.override cell in project p1.
AC-11 [unit] The regenerated role matrix denies Viewer's fleet.job.shell.escalate cell in project p1.

routing.reasoning: Deterministic additions across catalog mirrors and matrix snapshots, but risk defaults and policy floors are access-control behavior requiring strict isolated TDD.

AC-2's cell count goes from 221 to 223

userStories.title: Grant Developer narrowed bash decision authority
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the Developer seed and conditionally patch stored Developer roles with approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate.

**Motivation** — Building these four pieces first, with no production caller, lets `permissions-p3-approval-fleet` move both asks and drop `FleetApproval` without also changing the engine.

**Approach** — `apps/api/src/permissions/system-roles.ts`: the `developer` entries gain `'approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate'` directly after `'fleet.approval.decide.bash'` (which stays until the next feature).

Migration `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261106090000_approval_fleet_core/migration.sql` holds this statement. Whichever of US-002, US-003 and US-009 lands first creates the file and the others append their statements in landing order; any order is valid, since the three statements touch different tables:
```sql
UPDATE "Role"
SET "permissions" = "permissions" || '["approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate"]'::jsonb, "updatedAt" = NOW()
WHERE "key" = 'developer'
  AND "permissions" @> '["fleet.approval.decide.bash"]'::jsonb
  AND NOT "permissions" @> '["approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate"]'::jsonb;
```

Baseline (to locate the migration convention only): `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261105090100_drop_pending_action/migration.sql`.

**Developer now passes the plain `approval.decide` check in a project.** `PermissionService.can` grants `approval.decide` to any holder of an `approval.decide@<pattern>` entry (`holdsNarrowedDecide`), so Developer's project `approval.decide` cell in the role matrix flips from `not-granted` to `granted`. The routes that check it (`GET /approvals`, the decide route) are `enforcedBy: 'service'`, and `decideEligibility` still limits a Developer to `fleet.job.shell.escalate` requests. Its global cell stays `not-granted`.

**The stored Developer role is patched by the migration.** `SystemRoleSeeder` restores only locked roles from the seed, and Developer is unlocked, so the seed change alone never reaches an existing database. The migration appends `approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate` to the `developer` row's `permissions` when that row holds `fleet.approval.decide.bash` and does not hold the new entry. A Developer role an admin has already edited to drop bash deciding is left alone.

Verification note: the AC-4..7 statement is read from the migration file at test time (the test locates `20261106090000_approval_fleet_core/migration.sql` and extracts the `UPDATE "Role"` statement), so the test and the shipped SQL cannot drift. Update role-matrix.spec.ts AC-13's projectDecide.developer pin and regenerate __snapshots__/role-matrix.json with Vitest -u.

**Scope** — In: seed, stored-role SQL, idempotent migration behavior and Developer role-matrix project decide cell. Out: catalog additions (US-001), decision/execution eligibility implementation (US-007), params-column SQL (US-003), link-table SQL (US-009), and removing fleet.approval.decide.bash (next feature). Removing `fleet.approval.decide.bash` from the Developer seed: `permissions-p3-approval-fleet`.

**Interface** — The SQL statement above is the migration contract; the seed continues to use SYSTEM_ROLES and expandEntries(<developer entries>, 'PROJECT').
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] SYSTEM_ROLES' developer entries contain 'approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate', and expandEntries of them does not throw.
AC-2 [unit] Developer's entries still contain 'fleet.approval.decide.bash'.
AC-3 [unit] expandEntries(<developer entries>, 'PROJECT') contains 'approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate'.

AC-4 [integration] Given a developer role whose permissions are the seed without 'approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate', executing the migration's actual UPDATE via $executeRawUnsafe appends that entry exactly once at the end of its permissions array.
AC-5 [integration] Executing the same migration UPDATE a second time leaves that row's permissions unchanged.
AC-6 [integration] Executing the migration UPDATE leaves a developer row whose permissions lack 'fleet.approval.decide.bash' unchanged.
AC-7 [integration] Executing the migration UPDATE leaves a reviewer role row holding 'fleet.approval.decide.bash' unchanged.
AC-8 [unit] Developer's approval.decide role-matrix cell in project p1 is granted.
AC-9 [unit] Developer's global approval.decide role-matrix cell stays not-granted.

routing.reasoning: Seed, narrow conditional data migration and snapshot adjustment are conventional, but grant persisted decision authority and require the access-control security override.

userStories.title: Execute parsed decisions and run post-execution follow-up
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Re-parse stored approving params, pass the parsed decision to execution, and run warning-only afterCommit follow-up.

**Motivation** — A decision is more than approve or reject. A bash ask is answered `allow`, `allow_for_job` or `deny` (`apps/api/src/fleet/approvals/bash-decision.ts`). A budget ask is answered `keep_paused` or `raise_budget_and_resume` with an `amountUsd` and the cancelled jobs to re-queue (`ApprovalsService.decide`).

**Approach** — `ApprovalExecutionService`:
- The precheck gains a step after the input parse: when the command has `parseDecision`, it loads the request's decisions (`findDecisions`), takes the last one whose `decision` is `approve` (none after a timeout approval), and re-parses: `command.parseDecision('approve', stored?.params ?? undefined, parsed)`. A throw settles the request `failed` with `result: { error: 'invalid-decision' }`. `PrecheckFailure` gains `'invalid-decision'` and `Prechecked`'s ok branch gains `decision: unknown`.
- `run` calls `command.execute(parsed, decision)`.
- After `withCommittedEffects(...)` returns an `executed` record and the command has `afterCommit` (guaranteed after commit only when `execute` owns the transaction scope; inside an outer `withCommittedEffects` owner, such as the assistant executor's, it runs when that owner's callback returns), it awaits `command.afterCommit(parsed, decision, result)` inside a try/catch; a throw logs `approval request <id> after-commit failed: <message>` at warn and the settled record is still returned.

**Decision params are parsed at decide time and again at execution.** `parseDecision(decision, params, input)` validates the decider's params under the request lock, after eligibility (a caller who may not decide gets 403 whatever it sends), and its output is stored frozen in `ApprovalDecision.params`. The execution re-parses the stored value, as it re-parses the frozen input: `parseDecision` must accept its own output.

**`afterCommit` runs after the execution transaction commits, and its failure changes nothing.** It is for follow-up writes that need their own transactions (the budget re-queue, plan D232). A throw is logged as a warning; the request stays `executed`. It does not run after a `failed` settle.

Preserve the existing request lock, per-request serialization and distinction between callback failure and transaction open/commit failure. Keep the raw TResult for the hook, not the toResult projection stored in the request. Extend the existing helper to record the decision execute received and take an optional afterCommit; add findDecisions to execution-service repository doubles and extend the decision-params integration file authored by US-003.

**Scope** — In: execution precheck, invalid-decision settlement, optional execute argument, raw-result follow-up and warning isolation. Out: decide-time parsing/onReject/storage/interface declarations (US-003), SYSTEM authority skip (US-007), API params (US-005), actual budget requeue implementation or fleet command registration (next feature).

**Interface** — Verbatim hook signatures from the command contract supplied by US-003:
```ts
parseDecision?(decision: 'approve' | 'reject', params: unknown, input: TInput): TDecision;
/** `decision` is the approving decision's parsed params, or undefined when none were parsed. */
execute(input: TInput, decision?: TDecision): Promise<TResult>;
/** Runs after the execution transaction committed, under the request's context; a throw is logged only. */
afterCommit?(input: TInput, decision: TDecision | undefined, result: TResult): Promise<void>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] A request approved with params { remember: true } executes its command with decision equal to { remember: true }.
AC-2 [unit] A command with parseDecision executing a request approved without params receives the value returned by parseDecision('approve', undefined, input).
AC-3 [unit] The precheck calls parseDecision('approve', { remember: true }, input) when the request's only decision is an approve storing { remember: true }.
AC-4 [unit] Stored params refused by parseDecision at execution settle the request failed with result { error: 'invalid-decision' } without calling execute.
AC-5 [unit] A command without parseDecision executes with decision undefined without calling findDecisions.
AC-6 [unit] After an executed settle, afterCommit is called once with the parsed input, parsed decision and command's raw result.
AC-7 [unit] afterCommit is called after the transaction callback has returned, with its call order after txManager.run resolved.
AC-8 [unit] When afterCommit throws, the returned record remains executed and logger.warn receives a message starting 'approval request <id> after-commit failed:'.
AC-9 [unit] A command whose execute throws and whose request settles failed never has afterCommit called.

routing.reasoning: Runs authorized deferred commands across transaction and commit-effect boundaries; decision validation and settlement semantics require strict security TDD.

userStories.title: Expose decision params through REST and MCP
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Accept object params through the approval decide route and MCP tool and return stored params in decision DTOs.

**Motivation** — A decision is more than approve or reject. A bash ask is answered `allow`, `allow_for_job` or `deny` (`apps/api/src/fleet/approvals/bash-decision.ts`). A budget ask is answered `keep_paused` or `raise_budget_and_resume` with an `amountUsd` and the cancelled jobs to re-queue (`ApprovalsService.decide`).

**Approach** — **REST and MCP (US-005).** `DecideApprovalRequestDto` gains:
```ts
@ApiPropertyOptional({ type: Object, description: 'The decider\'s choice, when the action asks for one' })
@IsOptional() @IsObject()
params?: Record<string, unknown>;
```
`ApprovalRequestsController.decide` passes it: `this.decisions.decide(id, dto.decision, dto.comment ?? null, undefined, dto.params)`. `ApprovalDecisionDto` gains `@ApiProperty({ type: Object, nullable: true }) params!: unknown;`, mapped from `record.params`. The MCP tool `koda_decide_approval` adds `params: { type: 'object' }` to its input schema's properties and `'params'` to its allowed argument names; a present `params` that is not a plain object answers `invalid_input: params`. With `params` absent it calls `decide(args.id, args.decision, comment)` exactly as today; with it, `decide(args.id, args.decision, comment, undefined, args.params)`. `openapi.json` is regenerated with `bun run api:export-spec` (repo root) after this story.

Preserve route visibility checks, service-enforced eligibility and the Nathapp JsonResponse envelope; DTO validation refuses non-null, non-object params before any decision is persisted. REST params:null remains optional under @IsOptional and is normalized to absent by the service; MCP instead refuses every present non-plain-object params value, including null. Error handling is the US-003 mapping: `ApprovalDecisionParamsInvalidError('not-accepted' | 'too-large' | 'invalid')` becomes HTTP 400 `approvals.invalidDecisionParams`, and a forbidden decider remains 403 `approvals.decideForbidden`. Extend approval-http.spec.ts for params:null mapping, mcp/approval-mcp-tools.spec.ts for schema/allowlist/call arity, and the shared approval-decision-params.integration.spec.ts authored by US-003 for HTTP round trips. The regenerated spec adds params to the decide body and decision DTO, and no other operation changes.

**Scope** — In: DTO request validation and response mapping, controller forwarding, MCP input/schema forwarding and root OpenAPI regeneration. Out: engine decision parsing/persistence/error implementation (US-003), execution hooks (US-004), fleet command registration and /fleet/approvals adapters (next feature), web inbox and CLI formatting. The web inbox deciding fleet asks with params: P3 web. Showing decision params in the CLI (`koda approvals show` prints them as part of the detail JSON already; no new formatting).

**Interface** — The DTO declarations and exact service-call forms above are binding; MCP required remains ['id', 'decision'] and properties.params is { type: 'object' }.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] POST /approvals/:id/decisions with { decision: 'approve', params: { remember: true } } by an eligible decider returns 200 with the request's decision row storing params { remember: true }.
AC-2 [integration] The same route with params: { a: 1 } for a command without parseDecision returns 400 with the invalidDecisionParams message containing not-accepted.
AC-3 [integration] The decide route with params:'x' returns 400 from validation without creating a decision row.
AC-4 [integration] GET /approvals/:id for a request decided with params returns decisions[0].params equal to { remember: true }.
AC-5 [unit] ApprovalDecisionDto.from of a record with params:null returns params:null.
AC-6 [unit] koda_decide_approval's input schema properties.params equals { type: 'object' } and required is still ['id', 'decision'].
AC-7 [unit] Calling koda_decide_approval with { id: 'r1', decision: 'approve' } calls decide with exactly ('r1', 'approve', null).
AC-8 [unit] Calling koda_decide_approval with { id: 'r1', decision: 'approve', params: { remember: true } } calls decide with ('r1', 'approve', null, undefined, { remember: true }).
AC-9 [unit] Calling koda_decide_approval with params:[] returns invalid_input: params without calling decide.
FH-1 [unit] Calling koda_decide_approval with any present params value that is not a plain object returns invalid_input: params without deciding.

routing.reasoning: Adds standard optional DTO fields and argument forwarding to existing controller/MCP boundaries without a new abstraction; authorization-sensitive inputs still require the security-override strategy.

userStories.title: Authorize ask decisions without re-checking the system requester
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Generalize SYSTEM on-behalf-of eligibility and skip requester key re-checks only for non-assistant system asks, retaining cancellation refusal.

**Motivation** — They are raised by the system, not by a principal. A bash ask arrives in a runner report; a budget ask is opened by the budget evaluator when spend crosses a hard stop.

**Approach** — **Eligibility and execution (US-007).** `decideEligibility`: `isOnBehalf = request.actor.type === 'SYSTEM' && isSamePrincipal(decider, request.onBehalfOf)` (replacing the assistant-only comparison). `ApprovalExecutionService.recheckPrincipal` answers a new `'skip'` for a `SYSTEM` actor other than `assistant`, and `stillHoldsKey` answers true for it.

**The principal an ask is on behalf of counts as its own requester.** `decideEligibility` treats the on-behalf-of principal of any `SYSTEM` actor as it already treats the assistant's: a user contributes `human` and an agent `self`. A user deciding an ask of a job it requested is allowed (today's rule), and an agent deciding an ask of its own job contributes only `self`, which the default `agent` refuses (today's "no agent self-approval" ruling, US-006 of `permissions-p1d`).

**An ask is never re-checked against its actor's key at execution.** The re-check guards a principal whose permission was revoked while its request waited. An ask was not chosen by a principal: the decider's eligibility at decide time is the authority, and the command checks its own state when it runs (the job still `RUNNING` on the same lease; the budget policy still paused). `ApprovalExecutionService` skips the key re-check for a `SYSTEM` actor other than the assistant.

**No principal can cancel an ask.** `ApprovalDecisionService.cancel` compares the current actor with the requester, and a `SYSTEM` actor other than the assistant has no principal requester, so the cancel is refused (`ApprovalCancelForbiddenError`). This is today's code; an AC pins it.

The actor is SYSTEM/runner or SYSTEM/budget, not the job requester; onBehalfOf records that requester. A budget ask with onBehalfOf:null has no own-request exception and requires approval.decide or a matching narrowed decide entry. Keep action-key checks and distinct-approver semantics unchanged; direct humans satisfy any mode but do not gain unrelated-request decide permission. The skip must not affect SYSTEM/assistant: the assistant's onBehalfOf principal remains subject to permission-revoked. Only the two component/key pairs pinned by ApprovalAskService.open may create fleet asks, and no new production registration is made here.

Use open from US-006 for integration requests rather than manually fabricating request rows. US-007 AC-4 uses the real US-010 resolver for a budget ask, with no stubbed resolver. AC-6 uses Developer-bound users and US-002's seeded narrowed entry. Extend approval-eligibility.spec.ts, approval-execution.service.spec.ts and the ask integration spec created by US-006; keep existing assistant regression cases intact.

**Scope** — In: SYSTEM-wide onBehalfOf matching, non-assistant SYSTEM recheck skip and cancellation regression pin. Out: opening/closing implementation (US-006/008), resolver SYSTEM ranking (US-010), Developer seed (US-002), decision params and hooks (US-003/004), and production fleet command state checks (next feature). Re-checking the asker's key at execution (designer call above).

userStories.title: Close system asks as cancelled or expired
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement ApprovalAskService.close to settle pending system asks with a bounded reason and transactional request-change event.

**Motivation** — They close without a decision. A bash ask closes when its job leaves `RUNNING`. A budget ask closes when a newer hard stop supersedes it, its policy is deleted, its window resets or an admin resumes from the budgets page. The engine knows only expiry and the actor's own cancel.

**Approach** — `close` steps: no transaction → the step-1 error. `lockById`; null or `status !== 'pending'` → null. The request's actor is not `SYSTEM` or is `SYSTEM/assistant` → `Error('approval ask close: not an ask')`. `reason` empty or longer than 64 characters → `Error('approval ask close: invalid reason')`. As bookkeeping `approval.request-settle`: `transition(id, 'pending', { status, settledAt: now, result: { closedBy: reason } })`, record the event, answer the record. A lost transition under the lock throws `ApprovalRequestNotPendingError`.

The shared step-1 error is `Error('approval ask needs the caller\'s transaction')`.

**`open` and `close` join the caller's transaction and lock nothing themselves except the request row.** They do not call `txManager.run`: the fleet callers already hold the job or budget policy lock, and a nested `run` that throws poisons the outer transaction (the approval-assistant B1 finding, `PrismaTransactionManager`). A caller outside a transaction is a programming error and throws.

Close is bookkeeping, not a principal cancellation or decision: record one approval_request_changed outbox event in the same transaction, no AuditEntry and no decision row. It may close an already-overdue pending request as either caller-specified terminal status. Validate actor and reason only after the missing/nonpending early return, preserving idempotent null results. Use the service/spec and integration file created by US-006; this story does not author new files. No producer or closer is switched to call it here.

**Scope** — In: close implementation, request row locking, reason checks, CAS settlement and event bookkeeping. Out: open implementation/module registration (US-006), principal decide/cancel eligibility (US-007), link resolvedBy/outcome persistence (US-009), and production job/budget lifecycle callers (next feature).

**Interface** — Verbatim service method from the ask contract:
```ts
/** Inside the caller's transaction; null when the request is gone or not pending. */
close(requestId: string, close: { status: 'cancelled' | 'expired'; reason: string }, now?: Date): Promise<ApprovalRequestRecord | null>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] Inside txManager.run, close(id, { status: 'cancelled', reason: 'job_ended' }) on a pending ask returns the request with status cancelled.
AC-2 [integration] That closed request has settledAt equal to now and result { closedBy: 'job_ended' }.
AC-3 [integration] close(id, { status: 'expired', reason: 'timeout' }) returns status expired.
AC-4 [integration] Closing records one approval_request_changed outbox row whose metadata.eventId is '<id>:cancelled'.
AC-5 [integration] Closing writes no AuditEntry row.
AC-6 [unit] close returns null without calling transition when lockById returns null.
AC-7 [unit] close of an executed request returns null without calling transition.
AC-8 [unit] close of a request with actor SYSTEM/assistant rejects with Error without calling transition.
AC-9 [unit] close of a request with actor AGENT/a1 rejects with Error.
AC-10 [unit] close with reason '' rejects with Error.
AC-11 [unit] close with a 65-character reason rejects with Error.
AC-12 [unit] A transition returning null under the request lock causes close to reject with ApprovalRequestNotPendingError.
AC-13 [unit] close outside a transaction rejects with the same Error as US-006 AC-11, message "approval ask needs the caller's transaction".

routing.reasoning: A localized service addition with conventional locking and CAS, but it is a privileged settlement path that must refuse principals and assistant requests.

userStories.title: Resolve approval policy for a SYSTEM subject
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Widen resolver subjects with SYSTEM so system-owned asks use only pattern-only policies and catalog defaults without role lookup.

**Motivation** — They are raised by the system, not by a principal. A bash ask arrives in a runner report; a budget ask is opened by the budget evaluator when spend crosses a hard stop.

**Approach** — **Resolver (US-010).** `ApprovalSubject.type` widens to `ApprovalSubjectType | 'SYSTEM'`. For a `SYSTEM` subject `resolve` reads no role ids (as for `ASSISTANT`), `applicableSubjectRank` answers null for a role, type or principal policy and 3 for a pattern-only policy, and the fallback is `entry.approval.default`.

**The ask's subject is the principal it is on behalf of, or the system.** A bash ask is on behalf of the job's requester (`requestedByType`/`requestedById`, a user or an agent). It resolves with that principal as subject, so a policy for an agent or a role applies to the jobs that principal runs. A budget ask has no one on behalf: it resolves with a new subject type `SYSTEM` (the component id), which matches project and pattern policies only, like the rank-3 rule today, and never a role, type or principal policy. `SYSTEM` is not a policy subject a write can name (`ApprovalPolicyInput` is unchanged).

Keep current project/global precedence, specificity, strictest-mode tie-breaks and catalog floor enforcement. SYSTEM is not ASSISTANT: assistant retains its existing policy applicability and default human; SYSTEM may match project/global pattern-only policies and defaults from the catalog. Do not widen ApprovalSubjectType in the policy input/domain write union. It depends on US-001, which adds `fleet.budget.override` to the catalog.budget.override entry carrying the specified high-risk default agent and floor self; do not skip assertions or move production catalog changes into this story. Integration with the real catalog occurs after both foundations in US-006/007.

**Scope** — In: resolver-only subject type widening, no role lookup, subject ranking and regression pins for USER/AGENT/ASSISTANT. Out: catalog key definitions/defaults (US-001), passing SYSTEM subjects from open (US-006), decision eligibility (US-007), and SYSTEM as a writable policy subject (feature exclusion). `SYSTEM` as a policy subject a write can name.

**Interface** — Verbatim widening: `ApprovalSubject.type` widens to `ApprovalSubjectType | 'SYSTEM'`. The resolver continues to expose its existing resolve({ key, projectId, subject }) shape; ApprovalPolicyInput is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] resolve({ key: 'fleet.budget.override', projectId: P, subject: { type: 'SYSTEM', id: 'budget' } }) returns the mode of a project pattern-only policy for that key.
AC-2 [unit] For that SYSTEM subject, a project role policy for the key is ignored, returning source default when only that policy is present.
AC-3 [unit] For that SYSTEM subject, when the only candidate is a project type:AGENT policy for the key with mode human, resolve ignores it and returns source default with catalog default mode agent.

AC-4 [unit] For that SYSTEM subject, when the only candidate is a project principal:AGENT:budget policy for the key with mode human, resolve ignores it and returns source default with catalog default mode agent.
AC-5 [unit] With no policy, resolution returns catalog default agent.
AC-6 [unit] roleIdsAt is not called for a SYSTEM subject.

AC-7 [unit, regression pin] resolve retains the existing USER, AGENT and ASSISTANT cases in approval-policy.resolver.spec.ts unchanged: matching USER principal policies precede pattern-only policies at the same project/global scope; matching AGENT principal, role, type and pattern-only policies retain their existing project-before-global precedence, specificity, mode and id tie-break outcomes; ASSISTANT ignores pattern-only policies and defaults to human but matches explicit type:ASSISTANT policies.

routing.reasoning: A small resolver change, but subject policy applicability and fallback modes are security-critical access-control rules.

The registry validates catalog approvability and duplicate registration at :34. Add the third defaulted generic and optional hooks compatibly: existing assistant commands using two generics at apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/commands/assistant-tool.command.ts:28 must continue unchanged. - ApprovalGate at approval-gate.service.ts:51 accepts USER/AGENT or SYSTEM/assistant with onBehalfOf, refuses other system actors, directly executes mode none and direct humans, deduplicates pending inputs at :125, and owns a txManager.run at :135. A budget ask with no onBehalfOf needs a decide permission even for a human holding the action.
